figures.caption: Fig. 1 | Neural activity maps to models near criticality. a, Average activity m and correlation strength χ for 146 recordings of neuronal activity: 100 electrophysiological recordings from thalamus and visual cortex (blue),40, 41 45 calcium-imaging recordings from visual cortex (green),42 and one calcium-imaging recording from hippocampus (purple).43, 44 Marker size indicates the number of neurons N in each population. Gray line represents statistics that map to independent models (with λ = 0), defined by χ = 1−m2. b, Inferred Ising parameters h and λ for each of the recordings in a. Red line defines the set of critical models in the thermodynamic limit N → ∞, and gray line represents independent models (λ = 0). Inset displays the same parameters with a linear h axis, illustrating the collapse of the different recordings to critical models.

Fig. 2 | Expansion and contraction from parameters to statistics. a, Region in the space of parameters with color indicating the interaction strength λ and saturation indicating the external field h. Red line represents criticality in the thermodynamic limit. b, Regions in the space of statistics covered by the parameters in a for increasing numbers of neurons N . c, Scaling factor defined by the determinant of the Jacobian |J | increases monotonically as a function of the external field h. Each line represents N = 20 neurons interacting with a different strength λ. d, Jacobian |J | as a function of the system size N at fixed h = −10−3. For models near criticality (λ ≥ 1), the Jacobian grows dramatically with the number of neurons.

Fig. 3 | Large populations contract to critical models. a, Jacobian |J | as a function of the external field h and interaction strength λ. As the number of neurons increases, the Jacobian concentrates near the critical line. b, Flow in parameters due to a fractional increase in system size d(h,λ)

Fig. 4 | Models of neural activity flow toward criticality. a, Average activity m and correlation strength χ for subpopulations of increasing size N sampled from 146 recordings of neural activity from the thalamus and visual cortex (blue),40, 41 visual cortex (green),42 and hippocampus (purple).43, 44 Marker size indicates the number of neurons N in each subpopulation, and gray lines represent statistics that map to independent models. b, Inferred Ising parameters h and λ for each of the subpopulations in a. Red line defines the set of critical models in the thermodynamic limit N → ∞, and gray line represents independent models (λ = 0). Columns indicate populations of increasing size N = 20, 100, and 1000.

Fig. 5 | Collapse to criticality in the thermodynamic limit. a, Average activity m and correlation strength χ for the same recordings as Fig. 1. Red line defines the maximum correlations allowed under mean-field theory (Methods). Gray line defines statistics that map to independent models. Marker sizes indicate the number of neurons N in each population. b, Free energy f(µ) as a function of the population activity for subpopulations of increasing size sampled from the hippocampal recording.43, 44 See Methods for free energy expression. c-d, External field (c) and interaction strength (d) inferred for subpopulations of increasing size sampled from the thalamus and visual cortex (top),40, 41 visual cortex (middle),42 and hippocampus (bottom).43, 44 Markers represent exact parameters, solid lines represent the double-well approximation in Eq. (3), and dashed lines represent the thermodynamic limit of the double-well approximation. e, Double-well predictions for the external field and interaction strength [Eq. (3)] corresponding to the statistics in a with increasing population size N . As N → ∞, all recordings approach the critical line.
